relays.name: Altus-1 data-relay satellite
relays.status: Planned to fly alongside IM-3 (NASA, August 2026).
relays.orbit_note: NASA says only that Altus-1 is deployed 'in lunar orbit'. The orbit used here is assumed from NASA's reference design; where its node and its place along the orbit will be is swept.
relays.sweep_note: Worked out for 5184 placements of the relay: where its node sits and where it is along its orbit, on a 36 x 36 grid, at both ends of its assumed argument of periapsis and inclination. The range is the least and the most over those placements, the value their middle. Two-body orbit: Earth's pull turns a frozen orbit's node about half a degree a day, which the node sweep covers but a single placement does not follow.

longest_unheard_h.no_margin_reason: Its edges are set by station masks, which are published without a tolerance.

longest_message_wait_min.no_margin_reason: Set by the same edges as the longest time unheard, plus the light time to Earth.

data.relay_note: Numbers that use the relay are ranges over what its orbit could be, if it flies as planned; a message may wait on the relay until a ground station can hear it. The same two numbers without the relay are given beside them.

data.orbiters_note: A real orbiter's passes over the landing spot: when it could see the lander. None of these orbiters offers to relay for a lander; this is geometry, not a service.
data.link_budget_note: Line of sight only: the lander's radio power and data rate are not published, so no data rate or link margin is given.

parts.note: Earth's rise and set at the lander carry the skyline's timing margin; the ± on each number is those edges in quadrature.
DSN masks are published to a tenth of a degree without a tolerance; edges they set carry no margin here.
When a station can hear, not whether it is booked: the DSN's load is not modelled. Booked passes entered by the team are listed.
